files_reviewed: app/models/job.rb (criteria additions: latest_ai_job_criteria, latest_succeeded_ai_job_criteria, zero_criteria_extraction_failure?, extract_job_criteria_immediately, extract_job_criteria_if_needed, ai_job_criteria association)

findings.title: perform StandardError rescue can overwrite a terminal status/error_message set by ExtractCriteria and re-invoke broadcast_completion
findings.description: ExtractCriteria#extract catches its own JSON::ParserError/StandardError, sets the row to :failed with a specific error_message, and returns normally (extract_criteria.rb:148-156). Control then returns to perform which calls broadcast_completion (line 23). The entire perform body is wrapped by `rescue StandardError => e` (line 28). If broadcast_completion itself raises (e.g., a GlobalChannel/ActionCable failure) after a successful or already-failed extraction, this rescue re-reads the row and calls `update_columns(status: :failed, error_message: e&.message)` (line 33), clobbering the real extraction outcome/message (and thus potentially changing zero_criteria_failure? classification), then calls broadcast_completion again (line 34) which may raise a second time unhandled. This is structurally identical to the analog (generate_ai_job_application_summary_job.rb:39-45) and only triggers on a broadcast-layer exception, so it is an accepted edge case, not a feature defect — reported for completeness.
findings.recommendation: No change required (matches the adjudicated analog). If ever hardened, wrap the broadcast call in its own rescue so a broadcast failure cannot rewrite a completed row's status/error_message.

findings.title: Frontend in-flight spinner is never resolved when ExtractCriteria returns early without reaching a terminal status
findings.description: On the manual (requesting_organization_user_id present) path, if ExtractCriteria#extract returns early before writing a terminal status — e.g. `return unless @organization` (extract_criteria.rb:25-26) leaves the row `pending` — then broadcast_completion's `return unless ai_job_criteria.status_succeeded? || ai_job_criteria.status_failed?` (line 49) suppresses the broadcast. The completion event never fires, the payload never re-invalidates, and the frontend Regenerate button spins until a manual reload. These are degenerate states (a job with no organization) and the analog behaves identically (generate_ai_job_application_summary_job.rb:62). Reported for completeness; not a realistic user workflow.
findings.recommendation: No change required (matches analog). Would only matter if a job could legitimately reach extraction with a nil organization.

findings.title: extract_job_criteria_immediately issues two identical latest_ai_job_criteria queries
findings.description: `latest_ai_job_criteria` (job.rb:688, `ai_job_criteria.order(created_at: :desc).first`) is invoked twice in succession (lines 732 and 733) for the in_progress and retrying guards, firing two identical ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1 queries per call. Behavior is correct; this is a minor redundancy consistent with the original DECISIONS.md code block. Ordering matches the analog `has_one :latest_ai_job_application_summary, -> { order(created_at: :desc) }` (job_application.rb:32); with created_at precision:6 (schema.rb:187) a tie is effectively impossible for two sequential saves, so non-determinism is not a practical concern.
findings.recommendation: Optional: memoize the latest row into a local before the two guards. Not required.
